notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0104c.stoa001.opp-l: 268 completes a sentence begun before the unit ('nothing ... do the rivers, changed into red blood, compel'). 281: 'odio' is taken as 'foulness', the stench. '( simul)' is printed in round brackets in the text. 287 runs on into the next line ('all places').

nodes.text: the rivers, changed, compel; nothing the moving water,
fouled with a grim stench now the fish were dead,
because, girded with sinister chant,
the profane mind of [those] men was skilled in matching deeds.
Moreover they too make similar frogs creep forth
wherever there was land, wherever water, and they are created by matching
strains of the magicians' song; these, with rattling voice
croaking over everything, the prophet strove to drive away,
only not allowing the accustomed ones to be missing from the rivers.
This was offered to the king, if he wished to escape the plague
through the prayers of the old man as he prayed, so that thereafter it would be clear
that no other god reigns: the next day's light to the sky
is restored, and on that same day all [the frogs] are put to death,
and, heaped together, they rot away in bitter foulness.
Gnats are swiftly born over all the bodies
of four-footed beasts and of men (together), and the earth is filled.
This too the Chaldaean band, having attempted it, confesses
to be the hand of the Lord, and gives up its empty effort.
This done, the *cynomyia* flows in, which 'dog-fly'
is called, and at the prophet's nods it filled all
he will reckon them, to be promptly assessed, in the price of the hire.
If anyone takes for himself the use of a virgin not betrothed,
he shall join that same woman to himself as wife, with a dowry.
But if the mind of the girl he seized does not agree to the marriage,
let him give the father gifts such as are fitting for a marriage.
To hide a sorcerer is a sin. A hard death shall kill
the man mingled with a beast in the act of shameful coupling.
Let life leave the men who revere the shrines of demons,
since it is right to bow the neck to the Lord alone.
Let no one wrong a stranger by word or by hand:
